comment:purpose: The manifest. Adding a domain is one entry here, no code. `domain` / `docShape` / `queryShape` are REPORT metadata only — they never reach the ingest profile, whose vocabulary is frozen in packages/gnosis/src/config.ts.

datasets.comment: 42,139 of its 171,332 records carry a non-empty title and an EMPTY text — the CORD-19 metadata-only population, where the source never had an abstract, so nothing is lost in atom production. Before the T-04 projection fix those title-only atoms were all discarded as empty-bodied and the dataset FAILED the assertIngestSound 90% document-coverage gate; dropping them cost 3,135 relevant judgments (12.71%) across 50 of 50 topics, a hard recall ceiling of ~0.873. toMarkdown now gives a title-only record a non-empty chunk body, so the gate keeps them and this entry is enabled. IS in the `par` layer, against plan risk R4: R4 assumed a ~10 min ingest, but it MEASURES 270 s (4.5 min) and is cached in the work dir afterwards, making it cheaper than arguana (~11.6 min), which is uncontroversially Tier-1. Archive confirmed HTTP 200 at 73,876,720 bytes.

BEIR citation-prediction set: the query is a paper TITLE and the judged documents are the papers it cites, so it measures title→abstract matching rather than question→passage. Archive confirmed HTTP 200 at 142,471,588 bytes.

Financial-domain opinionated QA over StackExchange answers — the only Tier-1 entry whose documents are user-written forum prose rather than edited scientific text. Archive confirmed HTTP 200 at 17,948,027 bytes.

The id is the ARCHIVE id — touche2020.zip is a 404, and ensureBeirDataset resolves <dataDir>/<entry.id>/corpus.jsonl against the archive's inner directory, so the entry id MUST equal it. Kept deliberately as the rerank-REGRESSION control: it is the only BEIR dataset where a cross-encoder DEGRADES the result (published BM25 0.367 -> BM25+CE 0.271), so an arm that improves everything is measuring something other than reranking. `full`-ONLY, and that is measured rather than preferred: its ingest is 2,413 s (40 min) — 68% of the whole layer's cost — for 49 of the suite's 3,776 topics (1.3%), i.e. 1.2 topics/min against arguana's 121. Its value is the rerank regression above, which only `full`'s arms exercise, and it needs the 8 GB heap bench.sh now sets. Archive confirmed HTTP 200 at 227,132,363 bytes.

The same 103 biology queries as bright-biology, scored against the GOLD PASSAGES instead of the whole pages. A passage is ~387 chars, so one passage is essentially one atom and document-level scoring here IS block-level scoring — this is the block-ranking measurement. Its score MUST NOT be read as the cost of chunking relative to bright-biology: the candidate set is 57359 passages against 524 pages, so the two numbers measure different-difficulty tasks. To isolate chunking, vary atomMaxChars on ONE entry and compare across runs.

The REAL vault, the material dp-gnosis actually serves — every other entry is an English proxy. `derive` projects the ingested atoms plus the hand-authored golden set into the BEIR layout at `source` on EVERY run: both inputs are local files this repo already carries, so there is nothing to fetch and a cache could only measure a vault that has since changed. The atom FILENAME is the document id, which is what `relevantAtomIds` names and what `score.ts` recovers from `originPaths`.

The Hungarian half of the same material, against its own golden set. The recall ceiling is 1.0000 — all 117 judgments resolve (an older comment here claimed 22 were unreachable; that was a stale atom cache, re-measured 2026-08-15 as 0 unreachable). Its numbers are still NOT comparable with `vault` in absolute terms, for a different reason: 454 documents against vault's 11345 puts its random-ranking floor far higher (R@100 floor 0.2203 vs 0.0088), so compare only after normalising onto each corpus's own random-to-perfect scale.

Hungarian Wikipedia QA, converted from SzegedAI/MILQA (CC-BY-SA-4.0, SQuAD 2.0 layout). Exists for ONE reason: `vault-hu` carries 31 topics at an MDE of 0.05-0.07, which cannot decide any Hungarian analyzer or PRF question. This carries 16885 answerable questions over 2191 paragraphs, so its detectable effect is far smaller, and its random R@100 floor is 0.0456 against vault-hu's 0.2203. It is a LANGUAGE probe, not a product proxy: encyclopedic Wikipedia prose, not the served vault's technical notes, so a topical or domain conclusion MUST NOT be carried across. Unanswerable questions (28%) are dropped; the annotators deliberately paraphrased questions to avoid lexical matching, which is what makes it a real lexical-gap test rather than near-duplicate detection.

ROW X of the pre-rerank campaign — the query-phrasing ARM of `vault`. Identical corpus, identical topic ids, identical relevantAtomIds; ONLY the query text differs, rewritten to keyword form per packages/gnosis/README.md § Query rephrasing. The bench sends RAW query text, so phrasing — the largest measured quality lever in the system (P@10 0.20 -> 0.80) — is otherwise invisible to it; a committed rephrased golden file makes it a deterministic, perfectly paired experiment. `enabled` is FALSE on purpose: this is an arm, and enabling it would silently change what a bare `gnosis:bench` measures. Run it with `--only vault-rephrased`. 20 of the 60 topics are byte-identical to the base set by design (README rule 5 — MUST NOT dilute a query that already carries the exact rare term), so a whole-set delta is diluted by 33% guaranteed ties and the changed-topic subset MUST be reported alongside it.

AUTO arm of `vault` — the same 60 topics rewritten by the SHIPPED --rephrase path (packages/gnosis/src/rephrase.ts, qwen38-27b-q4kxl-ctx130k-mtp-coding, prompt v1) instead of by hand. Pairs against `vault` (what --rephrase buys) and against `vault-rephrased` (how much of the human ceiling it reaches). The tool rewrote 58 of 60 topics where the human deliberately left 20 untouched under README rule 5, so a whole-set delta here is NOT diluted by design ties the way the human arm is. Rewrites are frozen in the golden file, so the arm re-runs bit-identical without a model. `enabled` FALSE like the other arms; run with --only vault-autorephrased.

ROW X, Hungarian arm — the phrasing pair of `vault-hu`. All 31 topics are full inflected questions, so all 31 are rewritten; this is the cleaner half of the experiment. It also carries the README's non-English instruction (write the word STEM the document uses, not the inflected form the asker speaks), so it measures de-inflection and intent-stripping together, not separately. `enabled` FALSE for the same reason as `vault-rephrased`; run with `--only vault-hu-rephrased`.

AUTO arm of `vault-hu` — the same 31 topics rewritten by the SHIPPED --rephrase path (packages/gnosis/src/rephrase.ts, qwen38-27b-q4kxl-ctx130k-mtp-coding, prompt v1) instead of by hand. It exists so the tool is measured against BOTH its baseline and its human ceiling: `vault-hu` -> this is what --rephrase buys, this -> `vault-hu-rephrased` is how much of the hand-written ceiling it reaches. Rewrites are frozen in the golden file rather than called per run, so the arm is deterministic and re-runs bit-identical without a model. `enabled` FALSE for the same reason as the other arms; run with --only vault-hu-autorephrased.

F3 ablation, arm ONE of a pair — the DE-INJECTED half of `vault-hu-rephrased`, built to explain the +0.2407 gap the hand rewrite opens over the shipped `--rephrase` path on `vault-hu`, which no query-only mechanism accounts for. The provenance of the hand rewrite's 237 distinct terms was measured: 36.7% are retained verbatim from the question, 20.3% are de-inflected forms of a question term, and 43.0% are INJECTED — vocabulary traceable to no term of the question at all (`delivery_date`, `res.groups`, `ir.model.access`, `reverse charge`, `unmapped`, `excluded`). The hand set's own `variantNote` records that the corpus vocabulary was read once, globally, before rewriting, so injection is a capability the query-only `--rephrase` path structurally CANNOT have — it never sees the corpus. This arm keeps only the tokens that trace back to the base question, so de-inflection and intent-stripping are PRESERVED and injection alone is removed: the delta against `vault-hu-rephrased` prices the injected vocabulary, and the delta against `vault-hu` prices what is left. 99 of 216 surface tokens are dropped, and hu-023 falls back to its base question because every token of its hand rewrite was injected. MUST be read against `vault-hu-lengthcontrol`, never alone — a drop is otherwise ambiguous between provenance and length. `enabled` FALSE with `layers: []` on the same precedent as the four rephrased arms, so the default suite and every layered run are unchanged; run with `--only vault-hu-deinjected`.

F3 ablation, arm TWO of a pair — the LENGTH CONTROL for `vault-hu-deinjected`. It drops the same NUMBER of tokens per topic, but chooses them by a frozen FNV-1a hash of the token instead of by provenance. Without it a measured drop on the de-injected arm is ambiguous between two very different readings — "the injected corpus vocabulary was what earned the +0.2407" and "shorter queries simply score worse" — and only the first is a finding about rephrasing. Same 99 of 216 surface tokens dropped in count, same 31 topics, same relevantAtomIds, same corpus; hu-023 falls back to its base question here too, since its whole rewrite is dropped either way. The hash is frozen in the golden file rather than computed per run, so the arm re-runs bit-identical. Read the three-way spread `vault-hu-rephrased` -> this -> `vault-hu-deinjected`: if the two ablated arms land together, length explains the loss and injection buys nothing; if the de-injected arm lands materially higher, the injected vocabulary is the mechanism. `enabled` FALSE with `layers: []` on the same precedent as the four rephrased arms, so the default suite and every layered run are unchanged; run with `--only vault-hu-lengthcontrol`.
